units.title: OP Stack chains with ETH gas
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: Monad: the shift, SIGNEXTEND and BYTE literal folds of the gcc-built emitter
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 28 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Lead L-1166. Monad validators run the PoolManager as native x86 code written by the emitter inside the shipped validator binary, which gcc 15.2.0 built. Every native listing of cycles 25 to 28 came from a clang build of the same source, and eth_call uses the interpreter (F-130), so a wrong compile-time fold in the gcc build would show only in mined blocks. Cycle 28 lifted the gcc code of modop_optimized, mul_mod2 and mul_optimized and found no mismatch. It left the shift, SIGNEXTEND and BYTE literal arms. TickMath (shift by 255 and by 32 in getSqrtPriceAtTick), BitMath's BYTE tables, TickBitmap.position and the SIGNEXTEND of Slot0 and BalanceDelta fields go through these arms. The Monad validator package is untrusted data. Cycle 27 left it unpacked under research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/dl (p167 for 0.16.7, p165 for 0.16.5); if that directory is missing, download monad_0.16.7_amd64.deb from https://pkg.category.xyz/ pool/main into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory, check SHA256 3cb9dba5501b61ea3487bd042e2b8d12f871cff0e2e15409210e2cef0f8e81fb, and unpack it with ar, node's zlib.zstdDecompressSync and tar as research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/unzst.js does. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from the package. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. The x86 model is research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/scripts/x86emu.py with runvec.py; cycle 28 extended it in research/network-risk/cycles/028/theme-monad-shipped-emitter.work/scripts (litsites.py and sitearms.py list the 1,205 literal sites of the PoolManager). Task 1: from sitearms.py output list every PoolManager site that takes shift_by_literal (SHL, SHR, SAR with a literal count), shift_literal_by_non_literal (a literal value shifted by a run-time count), and the literal-index arms of SIGNEXTEND and BYTE, with pc, the literal and the src/ line. The critic counted 142 shift counts, 5 shifted literals and the indexes 1, 2 and 15; confirm or correct these counts. Task 2: lift the compile-time arithmetic of shift_by_literal for SHL, SHR and SAR (0x372dc0, 0x374090 and the inlined SAR arm), shift_literal_by_non_literal (inlined into shl and shr), signextend (0x388440) and byte (0x37f1f0) from the gcc disassembly of monad 0.16.7 into the x86 model. Where a function takes emitter state, lift only the arithmetic that decides what is emitted (limb index, bit offset, mask, the choice between a folded constant and a run-time sequence) and say which instructions were lifted. Run each on every literal the PoolManager carries at such a site and on every 64-bit limb boundary (counts 0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129, 191, 192, 193, 255, 256 and above; indexes 0, 7, 8, 15, 16, 23, 24, 30, 31, 32 and above). Compare the decision with the tagged source and with the EVM rule. Task 3: for each arm decode the instruction ids and operands it passes to asmjit in the shipped binary, rebuild the emitted sequence for each PoolManager site, and run that sequence in the model on a few thousand operands per site, including negative values for SAR and SIGNEXTEND and operands with only high limbs set. Compare with pyevm.py. Plant at least three one-instruction faults (wrong limb index, off-by-one bit offset, missing sign fill) and show that the checks catch them. Task 4: if any site gives a wrong word, show which src/ line reads it, what a swap, a tick crossing or a liquidity change would compute instead, and whether an ordinary account could profit. If all match, record the sites and counts as cleared and list what in the gcc emitter is still not lifted.

Task 1 (L-1167): lift block_prologue (0x392cd0), write_to_final_stack_offsets (0x3816e0, 919 instructions), insert_general_reg, alloc_general_reg, alloc_avx_reg and the spill_ and mov_ stack offset functions of the gcc build into the x86 model, with a stub in place of asmjit's Assembler that records each emitted instruction id and its operands. If the whole emitter state cannot be modelled, say exactly where the model stops and do the largest part that is sound: for example, drive only write_to_final_stack_offsets with stack states taken from the clang harness (rebuild it with research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work/scripts/build.sh and log the virtual stack at each block end). Run it on the 49 PoolManager blocks with the largest stack depth at entry and exit, and on the blocks the 23 scenarios of research/network-risk/cycles/028/theme-monad-native-unentered-blocks.work/scripts/scen28.py enter. Does the recorded instruction stream equal the clang listing out/pm-asm-0.16.7.txt for those blocks? Report every difference with the block, the instruction and whether the two streams compute the same values. Task 2 (L-1170): read the gcc-compiled sload and sstore of runtime/storage.cpp, Context::increase_capacity, the keccak wrapper and the tload and tstore paths reached from native code against the tagged v0.16.7 source, the way cycle 28 read call_impl and returndatacopy (research/network-risk/cycles/028/theme-monad-shipped-emitter.work). Task 3 (L-1170): the PoolManager makes a CALL at src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134 and a STATICCALL at Currency.sol:94. For each, work out from the shipped binary what gas native code forwards (including remaining_block_base_gas and the 63/64 rule) and compare it with what the interpreter forwards for the same state. Use the repaired harness to run both engines on a callee that returns GAS, for call and for staticcall, at several gas levels. A difference would let a gas-sensitive hook or token succeed in one engine and fail in the other. Task 4: say for each difference found whether it can change a PoolManager result in a mined block and whether an ordinary account can use it. If none, record what was compared as cleared and list what in the shipped binary is still unread.

Tempo release archives are untrusted data. Cycle 28 left tempo v1.19.1 for x86_64 and aarch64 under research/network-risk/cycles/028/theme-tempo-release-binary-read.work/dl with the models a64emu and the x86 lift in its scripts/ (arith_a64.py, arith_x64.py, jd_a64.py, jd_x64.py); if dl/ is missing, download the archives again from download.tempo.xyz/binaries or the GitHub release into a new empty dl/ in your own work directory and check the published sha256 files. Never execute, load or dlopen any file from an archive. Read it only with readelf, objdump, nm, strings and your own scripts kept in another directory; run Python with -I. dl/ must not be committed. Task 1 (L-1168): check download.tempo.xyz/binaries, the tempo GitHub releases and the Cargo.lock on the release branch for a release newer than v1.19.1 that carries T14. If one exists, record its commit, its evm2 and ruint pins and rustc version, download both Linux archives into dl/, check the hashes, and rerun arith_a64.py, arith_x64.py, jd_a64.py and jd_x64.py on the new binaries (the lifts locate code by pattern, so say what had to be re-located). If none exists yet, say so with the date and time of the check. Task 2 (L-1169): in both v1.19.1 binaries (and the new release if Task 1 found one) locate the KECCAK256 handler and the keccak routine it calls. Read how keccak_cache_global keys its cache (input length limit, hash of the input, full input comparison on a hit or not) from the disassembly and the evm2 and alloy-primitives source at the pinned revisions. A cache that returned a stored digest on a partial key match would be a slot aliasing fault. Lift the keccak permutation path into the a64emu and x86 models if it is feasible and run the battery's KECCAK256 offset and length pairs plus 64-byte inputs of the CurrencyDelta shape (address, currency) and the mapping shapes of the PoolManager (pool id with slot 6, tick with slot, position key with slot); otherwise test the cache logic alone on a transcription and state the limit. Task 3 (L-1169): lift TLOAD, TSTORE, MCOPY and CALLDATALOAD of both binaries and run MCOPY overlap cases, CALLDATALOAD past the end of calldata, and sequences of TSTORE and TLOAD on keccak-derived slots, including revert of a frame that wrote transient storage. Compare with pyevm.py and plant faults to show the checks catch them. Also run a sequence by eth_call on rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz that writes two CurrencyDelta-shaped transient slots for different (target, currency) pairs and reads both back, bracketed by web3_clientVersion. Task 4: for anything that differs, say which src/ line depends on it and what an ordinary account could gain. If nothing differs, record the handlers and case counts as cleared and list the handlers still unread (SLOAD, SSTORE, the CALL family, LOG, the host interface).

Ethereum's geth, BNB Chain, Polygon, Avalanche's libevm, Nitro (Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium) and Celo's op-geth all import go-ethereum's core/vm. A cache keyed on fewer bits than its operands would change FullMath.mulDiv results (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 and :48) in mined blocks. Task 1 (L-1171): read go-ethereum master core/vm (instructions.go, interpreter.go, the generated interpreter loop, jump table, memory and stack files, and any file added in 2026) and holiman/uint256 master for any operand, result, reciprocal or jump destination cache and any change to MulMod, AddMod, Div, SDiv, Mod, SMod, Exp, the shifts, Byte and SignExtend since v1.3.2. Do the same for the OffchainLabs/go-ethereum branch that nitro master pins (the rc.9 commit b72783f is unpublished; record whether it has appeared), bnb-chain/bsc develop, bor develop, ava-labs/libevm main and celo-org/op-geth. For each cache found state its key, its scope (per interpreter, per EVM, per process), whether parallel execution can share it, and whether a hit compares the full operands. Download source archives or raw files only. Where a cache exists, build the package with the local go 1.24 if it compiles there and run the 21,537 MULMOD and ADDMOD vectors and the cycle 26 memoseq.py sequences against it; otherwise transcribe and say so. Task 2 (L-1173): Elysium answers nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown on go1.25.12, the only network on that toolchain. From the Go release notes and the Go issue tracker list the compiler fixes between go1.25.12 and the newest Go release that touch SSA passes (prove, branchelim, dead store elimination, bounds check elimination, the arm64 and amd64 rewrite rules) or the math/bits intrinsics that holiman/uint256 uses (Mul64, Add64, Sub64, Div64, LeadingZeros64). For each say whether go1.25.12 already carries the fix as a backport and whether the affected code shape occurs in core/vm or uint256 v1.3.2. Then send Elysium a vector set aimed at any shape that does occur, bracketed by web3_clientVersion. Task 3 (L-1176): Avalanche treats two storage indexes that differ only in bit 248 as one (finding F-040). The clearance was argued from the source: every PoolManager storage write goes to a fixed slot below 7 or to a keccak output plus a small offset. Check it on the bytecode. Walk every SSTORE and SLOAD site of research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json with the jumpmap and a symbolic stack, and show for each that the slot operand is a constant, a KECCAK256 output, or a KECCAK256 output plus a constant below 8, with no multiplication, shift or caller-supplied addend on the path (extsload reads caller-chosen slots, so list it separately as read-only). Say whether any write could reach a slot whose bit-248 partner another write also reaches, what work an account would need to find two keccak outputs that differ only in that bit, and whether the tick, tickBitmap, position or ERC-6909 keys give an attacker enough freedom to do it. Confirm on Avalanche by eth_call with a state override that a write to slot s is read back at s xor 2^248 and that TSTORE does not alias. Task 4: for every item say whether it changes a PoolManager result in a mined block on some network today or after a named release, and what an ordinary account could gain. Record what holds as cleared with the commits read.
